intro: The て-form is a joint: it hooks one clause onto the next without saying much about how they relate. Bare て means "and (then)". Add も and the link becomes "even if": the result holds anyway. Add は and it becomes "if you do that (it's bad)", the source of てはいけない "must not". The stem is the same in all three: 飲んで, 飲んでも, 飲んでは.

skills.rule: The て-form joins clauses: "A and (then) B". The clauses come in the order things happen, and tense and politeness are carried only by the last verb.
skills.explain:
Forming it: verbs in -う, -つ, -る become って; -む, -ぶ, -ぬ become んで; -く becomes いて and -ぐ becomes いで; -す becomes して. Ichidan verbs drop る and add て (食べて). する is して, 来る is きて, and 行く is the exception: 行って. i-adjectives use くて (安くて); nouns and na-adjectives use で (学生で, 静かで). So て and で are one particle.

Uses: sequence (起きて、顔を洗う), manner or means (歩いて行く "go on foot"), a mild cause (風邪をひいて、休みました), and plain linking of descriptions (安くておいしい). After a cause with て, the second clause cannot be a request, invitation or intention; use から for those.

と also means "and", but only between nouns. It never joins verbs, adjectives or clauses. ながら means two actions at the same time; てから stresses "only after".

examples.jp: 朝[あさ]起[お]き{て}、シャワーを浴[あ]びます。
examples.en: I get up in the morning and take a shower.

examples.jp: この店[みせ]は安[やす]く{て}おいしい。
examples.en: This place is cheap and good.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]まで歩[ある]い{て}行[い]きました。
兄[あに]は医者[いしゃ]{で}、姉[あね]は教師[きょうし]です。
examples.en: My older brother is a doctor, and my older sister is a teacher.

examples.jp: 本[ほん]を読[よ]ん{で}、感想[かんそう]を書[か]いてください。
examples.en: Please read the book and write your thoughts on it.

examples.jp: 風邪[かぜ]をひい{て}、学校[がっこう]を休[やす]みました。
examples.en: I caught a cold and stayed home from school.

contrast.note: と joins nouns only (パンと牛乳). Between adjectives or verbs, "and" is always the て-form.
ながら is "while", two actions at once by the same person (歩きながら話す). て puts them one after the other.
て can show a mild cause, but not before a request or "let's": 雨だから、タクシーで行こう, not 雨で、タクシーで行こう.

mistakes.bad: この店[みせ]は安[やす]いとおいしいです。
mistakes.good: この店[みせ]は安[やす]く{て}おいしいです。
mistakes.note: と never joins adjectives. i-adjectives link with くて.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]の家[いえ]に行[い]いて、遊[あそ]びました。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]の家[いえ]に行[い]っ{て}、遊[あそ]びました。
mistakes.note: 行く is the one -く verb whose て-form is 行って.

mistakes.bad: この公園[こうえん]は静[しず]かくて、きれいです。
mistakes.good: この公園[こうえん]は静[しず]か{で}、きれいです。
mistakes.note: na-adjectives and nouns link with で, not くて.

skills.tip: Read て as "and" and keep the events in order; put the tense on the last verb only.

skills.rule: て-form + も means "even if / even though": the second clause holds no matter what the first says.
skills.explain:
Forms: 飲んでも, 食べても, 高くても, 学生でも, 静かでも. Negative: 行かなくても "even if I don't go".

Three common patterns. Concession: 雨が降っても、試合はあります "even if it rains, the match is on". Permission: てもいい(です) "it's all right to", てもいいですか "may I?", and なくてもいい "you don't have to". Question word + ても, "no matter": 何を食べても, いくら探しても, どんなに頑張っても.

ても covers both the hypothetical ("even if it rains tomorrow") and the factual ("even though I took medicine, the fever didn't go down"). のに also means "even though", but only for facts known to be true, with surprise or complaint; it cannot express a hypothetical "even if".

The edge is the conditionals. たら, ば and と say the result follows from the condition; ても says it does not depend on it. 雨が降ったら行きません "if it rains, I won't go" against 雨が降っても行きます "even if it rains, I'll go".
patterns: [i-adj く て] も / [noun] で も
[verb て] も いい です (か)

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]っ{ても}、試合[しあい]はあります。
examples.en: Even if it rains, the match will go ahead.

examples.jp: 窓[まど]を開[あ]け{ても}いいですか。
明日[あした]は来[こ]なく{ても}いいですよ。
examples.en: You don't have to come tomorrow.

examples.jp: 高[たか]く{ても}、このかばんが欲[ほ]しいです。
examples.en: Even if it's expensive, I want this bag.

examples.jp: 薬[くすり]を飲[の]ん{でも}、熱[ねつ]が下[さ]がらない。
examples.en: Even though I took medicine, my fever won't go down.

examples.jp: いくら考[かんが]え{ても}、答[こた]えが分[わ]かりません。
examples.en: No matter how much I think about it, I can't work out the answer.

contrast.note: These are "if": the result depends on the condition. ても is "even if": the result happens regardless. Swapping them reverses the meaning.
のに is only for real facts and carries frustration (薬を飲んだのに…). For a hypothetical "even if" (もし…), only ても works.

mistakes.bad: 高[たか]いでも、買[か]います。
mistakes.good: 高[たか]く{ても}、買[か]います。
mistakes.note: i-adjectives form ても as くても. でも follows nouns and na-adjectives.

mistakes.bad: いくら探[さが]したら、見[み]つかりません。
mistakes.good: いくら探[さが]し{ても}、見[み]つかりません。
mistakes.note: Question word + "no matter how" takes ても, not たら.

mistakes.bad: もし明日[あした]雨[あめ]が降[ふ]るのに、行[い]きます。
mistakes.good: もし明日[あした]雨[あめ]が降[ふ]っ{ても}、行[い]きます。
mistakes.note: もし makes the condition hypothetical. のに only takes a known fact, so a hypothetical "even if" needs ても.

skills.tip: Can you put "even" in front of the English "if" or "though"? Then it is ても.

skills.rule: て-form + は sets up a condition that leads to a bad result; its everyday use is てはいけない / てはだめ, "must not".
skills.explain:
Forms: 食べては, 撮っては, 飲んでは (ん-stems give では). In casual speech ては contracts to ちゃ and では to じゃ: 食べちゃだめ, 飲んじゃだめ.

Prohibition is the core use: ここで写真を撮ってはいけません "you must not take photos here". だめ is the conversational version and ならない the formal one used for rules and laws. It is the mirror of てもいい: てもいい permits, てはいけない forbids. Keep the pairs together; ても + いけない is not a prohibition, and ては + いい is simply wrong.

Outside prohibition, A ては B means "if A, then B (and that is bad)": そんなに働いては、体を壊しますよ "if you work that hard, you'll ruin your health". B is always unwelcome: a warning, a complaint or an impossibility (こう暑くては、眠れない). For a neutral or good result, use たら or と instead.
patterns: [verb て] は いけません / だめ です
[verb て] は ならない (rules)

examples.jp: ここで写真[しゃしん]を撮[と]っ{ては}いけません。
examples.en: You must not take photos here.

examples.jp: 授業中[じゅぎょうちゅう]に寝[ね]{ては}だめですよ。
図書館[としょかん]で大[おお]きい声[こえ]で話[はな]し{ては}いけません。
examples.en: You must not talk loudly in the library.

examples.jp: この薬[くすり]は一度[いちど]にたくさん飲[の]ん{では}いけない。
examples.en: You must not take a lot of this medicine at once.

examples.jp: そんなに働[はたら]い{ては}、体[からだ]を壊[こわ]しますよ。
examples.en: If you work that hard, you'll wreck your health.

examples.jp: こんなに暑[あつ]く{ては}、眠[ねむ]れない。
examples.en: I can't sleep when it's this hot.

contrast.note: てもいい gives permission; てはいけない forbids. The particle decides which, so do not mix them.
たら and と are neutral "if / when". ては predicts or complains about a bad outcome.
Bare て cannot make a prohibition: 撮っていけません is wrong. The は is required.

mistakes.bad: ここで写真[しゃしん]を撮[と]ってもいけません。
mistakes.good: ここで写真[しゃしん]を撮[と]っ{ては}いけません。
mistakes.note: Prohibition is ては + いけない. ても pairs with いい.

mistakes.bad: 写真[しゃしん]を撮[と]ってはいいですか。
mistakes.good: 写真[しゃしん]を撮[と]っ{ても}いいですか。
mistakes.note: Asking permission is てもいいですか. ては never goes with いい.

mistakes.bad: お酒[さけ]を飲[の]んでいけません。
mistakes.good: お酒[さけ]を飲[の]ん{では}いけません。
mistakes.note: Without は there is no prohibition; after ん, ては becomes では.

skills.tip: Forbidding or warning of trouble? ては. Allowing? ても. いい goes with も, いけない goes with は.
